newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley to meet with Rainbow-PUSH.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley to meet with Rainbow-PUSH.

text.p: Commercial printer R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co said Sunday it will meet with the Rev. Jesse Jackson's Rainbow PUSH Action Network on Monday to address complaints of racism and age discrimination.

"The company values its reputation as a good employer that treats all employees fairly and equally, regardless of their position in the company," R.R. Donnelley said in a statement. The company said it does not tolerate discrimination of any type.
R.R. Donnelley, a commercial printing company, is the target of a $500 million federal class-action lawsuit that alleges racial discrimination based on layoffs, promotions and wages.
The company had said the lawsuit was filed in connection with a 1993 plant closing and it denies the allegations, labeling them as "reckless, false and inflammatory."

The operation was closed as a result of Sears, Roebuck & Co.'s decision to discontinue its twice a year "big-book" catalogues, which represented the primary work performed at the facility, the company said.
